newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebel leader says controls mining area.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebel leader says controls mining area.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Monday his forces had captured the gold and diamond mining centre of Kamituga on his southern front, as well as the town of Beni on the northern front.

Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for Liberation of Congo-Zaire, which now controls much of eastern Zaire, told reporters that on the northern front his group was advancing beyond Beni in pursuit of fleeing Zairean troops.
"On the northern front we are still advancing, Beni has fallen. Today is the second day of our control of Beni," Kabila said in the rebel-held lakeside city of Bukavu.
"In the south we have now got Kamituga town, we have been there for two days now," Kabila added.

He said some 700 Zairean soldiers aided by Rwanda's former Hutu army had fled Beni. "Villagers in Beni complained to our forces of extensive rapings, beatings and killings by the fleeing soldiers," he added.

The latest round of the conflict in central Africa began in October when the Banyamulenge, an ethnic Tutsi group which first came to Zaire from Rwanda nearly 200 years ago, rebelled against the government's attempt to repatriate them.
